episodes.title: Jensen Huang’s Nvidiotic Spy Scandal + Can Dems Pass AI Regulation?
episodes.about: It might be the biggest tech scandal of the year, and possibly the most significant intelligence breach since the Cold War. On Sunday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair, following reports that Alice Huang, the woman involved, is a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. What happens now to Jensen, to the world's most important AI company (which has no clear succession plan), and to the fight over U.S.-China AI policy and chip export controls? Then, Rep. Greg Casar of Texas, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and one of the most vocal voices on AI regulation in the House, joins to talk about how Democrats plan to use their new majority to pass AI policy, why he wants to tax AI companies, and why he co-wrote a bill with Sen. Bernie Sanders to ban artificial superintelligence.
episodes.why: Always-include show: Jensen Huang admitted the affair and the other Huang is a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, with no succession plan at Nvidia — then Rep. Casar on taxing AI companies and banning recursive self-improvement.

episodes.title: AlphaGenome 2: Teaching AI to read the entire human genome
episodes.about: AlphaGenome 2 is Google DeepMind's next-generation DNA sequence model, announced November 11. Where the first AlphaGenome predicted how DNA variants affect molecular activity across broad tissues, AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional model: it takes a specific cell type or cell state as input alongside a million-letter DNA sequence and predicts that variant's effect in that one kind of cell. Trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues, it identifies nearly twice as many variants that change gene expression in cells as the previous state of the art, and it can analyze cell types and disease states it has never seen before, without retraining. It is available now for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — DeepMind's own research podcast, new here: AlphaGenome 2, announced yesterday, predicts what a single-letter DNA change does in one specific cell type instead of a tissue average, and reproduced an IBD finding in gut immune cells.

episodes.title: The Next Era of Games: Mods, Agents, and Infinite Worlds
episodes.about: AI is collapsing the distance between an idea and a playable game. What happens when almost anyone can build one? In this episode, a16z General Partners Anish Acharya and Jonathan Lai discuss how AI is changing game development, from generating art and code to operating tools like Blender and game engines directly. They explain why cheaper development could let studios take more creative risks while opening game creation to people without traditional coding or design skills. They also explore modding, remixing existing games, and the emergence of AI-native experiences that generate characters, abilities, and storylines on the fly, potentially creating games that never really end.
episodes.why: Out today: a16z's games partners on agents that do not just generate art and code but operate Blender and game engines themselves, and on AI-native games that generate characters and storylines on the fly.

episodes.title: Agents That Think Together: Cisco's Vijoy Pandey on Semantic Alignment, Scope, Accord & Concord
episodes.about: Vijoy Pandey, SVP and GM of Outshift by Cisco, discusses the challenges of multi-agent systems and Cisco's new open-source protocols designed to help AI agents collaborate effectively. He explains how tools like Scope, Accord, and Concord address semantic misalignments, intent negotiation, and cognitive failures across complex workflows. The conversation also dives into personal agent setups, avoiding model lock-in, and the rise of latent space communication. Finally, Pandey shares why proper guardrails will ensure humanity benefits as autonomous systems grow in complexity.
episodes.why: The long one: Pandey on why multi-agent systems fail on meaning before they fail on capability — agents using the same words for different things — and the open-source Scope, Accord and Concord protocols built to fix that.

episodes.title: Inside the Jeff Bezos-Backed Startup Trying to Automate Engineering
episodes.about: Physical AI, or the move of AI from digital to the physical world, is considered one of tech's next frontiers. At a recent WSJ Tech event, WSJ reporter Kate Clark sat down with Prometheus co-CEO Vik Bajaj to discuss moving beyond large language models to speed up real-world construction, manufacturing competition with China, and the startup's $41 billion valuation. Julie Chang hosts.
episodes.why: Thirteen minutes, out today: Prometheus co-CEO Vik Bajaj on moving past language models to AI that speeds up construction and manufacturing, and on competing with China in the physical world.
